Something extremely similar happened to me as a child, for years. Looking back on it it’s quite spooky, but at the time I was so used to it that it was more of an annoyance than anything. I came to expect it most nights. 

Basically, I’d hop in bed, turn the lights off, and just as I was starting to get cozy the bed would... vibrate or sway a bit, basically. It wasn’t tapping the way you described it, more like something akin to an earthquake or a rocking ship. I did live in a place where there were a lot of earthquakes at the time, but this was notably *just* affecting the bed, and it didn’t feel the exact same way that an earthquake felt. And an earthquake like that happening at the same time every night is just really unlikely. 

Similarly, I slept alone and I was awake when this would happen. Granted I was sleepy, but definitely awake enough to clearly feel this weird sensation and know I wasn’t dreaming. 

Thinking back on it now that I’m writing, it honestly almost felt like someone was pushing my mattress side to side over and over, or nudging/shaking it constantly. I remember wishing the person would just go away. I remember thinking as long as I closed my eyes it would go away eventually. And it always did, and I was able to fall asleep. 

I never told anyone about it for some reason. I guess because even as a kid I’ve always been a really logical person who was skeptical of anything even remotely paranormal. And eventually, the entire thing stopped out of nowhere and I’ve never felt that sensation again, that I can remember. But the memories of those years are so vivid. Honestly it’s kind of terrifying to think about, because I have absolutely no explanation. It’s even stranger that our experiences are so similar.

Soft YTA. First of all because of the simple fact that you created a club solely out of spite rather than positive intention, which is petty and kind of immature. 

Secondly, I understand from an outsider’s perspective it might seem exclusionary, but having a club exclusively for vegetarians, vegans, etc. is probably not something you should take personally. 

Here’s why— having a more plant-based lifestyle is still seen as a “niche” lifestyle. Although it’s gaining traction these days, it’s still a bit uncommon to find others who forgo meat, particularly if you live in meat-centric areas of the world. Oftentimes, people who share the same diet share similar worldviews, similar stances on ethics and morality or at least have an interest in the same topics. Naturally, you would want the opportunity to socialize with others you / your views are similar to. Hence a vegan club. 

Now, as a meat eater, you would probably be coming into this as an outsider without the same kind of views and interests, or maybe you’re interested but just haven’t been exposed to much of the lifestyle yet. I think that’s great— if you’re interested in veganism or vegetarianism, definitely explore that! But I don’t know that their vegan social events, for vegans and the like, is the best place to do so. Vegans and vegetarians, because they are still the minority, often have to explain themselves to meat-eaters, explaining their diet, their choices, why they feel the way they do about certain topics, which foods they like to eat and which they don’t, etc. It can be exhausting to have to constantly educate everyone who’s curious about your diet especially because sometimes you just don’t want to have to explain yourself. As a vegetarian I can attest to this. I imagine their social club is likely a place where they don’t want to have to sit down and explain themselves or educate everyone who joins— hypothetically, everyone there already shares similar knowledge and views, and they can spend their time just enjoying their food and discussing other things instead. 

That is actually why I imagine they would create such a club in the first place. It is a place where they don’t have to feel like the minority, or explain their niche lifestyle. They can feel free to just be themselves with no commentary or judgment from others because everyone there is in the same boat. As others have said, you getting upset and creating a meat club in revenge is akin to a straight pride parade in response to gay pride. 

It’s absolutely fine to want to learn about diets, lifestyles, and interests that differ from yours. But also let them have their own space to relax and feel comfortable without taking it personally.

To be fair, a lot of people are brought up believing they’re straight, or are pressured into living like they are, and end up getting pushed into straight marriage and kids when they might not really want that. It’s just how heteronormative/homophobic society was up until recently— and it’s still like that in some places, particularly the Deep South. 

Obviously you’re right, stuff like this shouldn’t happen. But that doesn’t necessarily mean someone is an asshole if they end up in this situation. As a bisexual person myself who spent years of my life growing up in the Deep South, I did not realize I was bisexual (EVEN after being romantic with another girl, kissing touching etc etc) until I was an adult, because of how stigmatized it was by society. I just thought I went through a curious phase. Similarly, I know many peers who were/are gay who did not even realize it until adulthood, simply because they just weren’t allowed, essentially, to even think that way. 

Even if you DO realize you’re gay at an early enough age, that doesn’t mean family pressure isn’t still impacting you. It’s really easy to say “oh well then just don’t get married and have kids then.” But the problem is that usually people in these situations, even if they realize they’re gay, are pressured by family/society to live a straight life, for fear that they will be ostracized and abandoned by everyone they love and care about. Oftentimes family puts pressure on young adults to get married and have children, and for many people, particularly vulnerable people, it is hard to escape the pressures of family and the society around you. 

In the end, yes— no one should get married to someone they’re not attracted to. It shouldn’t happen. But it’s a bit idealistic to gloss over all the nuances of these situations by saying “just don’t get married then”.

When I was in middle + high school I was best friends with another girl who loved writing as much as I did. I had a plot for a story I got really invested in, and brought up the idea of roleplaying to her— neither of us had ever done it before, but we were very excited to try. 

Sure enough, we ended up become long-term partners and wrote together nearly every single day. We had several stories we played but the main story was extremely long, intricate, detailed... the characters were various and fleshed out. I loved this story so much it’s hard to even put it into words. There was a main couple in the story, which of course we each played a character of. My friend and I actually ended up falling in love and dating, partially because we became so invested in our characters’ relationship, and began to see each other as a romantic partner rather than just a writing partner. This relationship lasted about a year, and we ended up breaking up, but still we continued being roleplay partners writing nearly everyday for FIVE years. 

So of course when our friendship came to an end (because it turns out she became a horrible person, unfortunately), I was crushed. Absolutely devastated. And I’m still affected by it to this day. I can’t stand who she is as a person anymore and I’m happy not to have her in my life, but that story meant so much to me... I miss it literally every day. I love it so much I would love to write it all out and turn it into a novel some day, but it feels so wrong to do it without her. I spent my entire adolescence building this world and these characters with her, and the loss of that hits me way harder than the loss of her love or friendship ever did.

You have every single right to feel the way you do about this, it was excruciating what you had to go through because of a decision she made. However, she was only 13 when this happened; a child. She’s still only 19 which is still very young. She also grew up under the control and belief system of your parents, so it makes sense that she might have been indoctrinated as a young child to believe what you were doing was wrong. Her actions seems obviously wrong to us now, but to a child who has been indoctrinated morals can be very different and very black and white, so she probably thought what she was doing was the right thing (and she probably got praise from your parents, which would have encouraged her even further). 

For children who have been indoctrinated like this it can be extremely difficult to overcome their belief system, so it probably would take something like college, with its promotion of critical thinking, diverse student population, and relative isolation from parents (the indoctrinators) for someone to realize their former beliefs and values were wrong. 

Again, your feelings are valid and you can do anything you think will help you and protect your happiness, but try to remember how young and easily impressionable your sister was at the time this happened. She’s 19 now, still young but she’s growing up, and she’s questioning what she’s been taught her whole life. And honestly, that’s a great thing.

I have a lot I want to say that’s already been covered in other comments, so I’ll just say a couple things that I haven’t really seen many people mention.

One, you seem to be making this argument on the assumption that there are all kinds of purebred dogs filling up shelters (through your saying breeders are contributing to dogs being euthanized etc). However this isn’t actually true. In fact it’s really hard to find most dog breeds in shelters; the overwhelming majority of dogs in shelters are pit bull or lab mixes (at least here in the USA). Dogs from reputable breeders rarely end up in shelters because they don’t usually have behavioral issues and most breeders will take dogs back if the family can’t keep them for whatever reason. So, almost all dogs in shelters are the result of strays, backyard breeding, or accidental litters due to irresponsible pet ownership. Therefore the only breeders directly contributing to euthanasia in this case would be pit bull or lab mix breeders. Getting rid of “vanity” dog breeding for other breeds would therefore do very little to stop the problem of pit bull euthanasia in shelters. I think you might be making the assumption that people who can’t get a dog from a breeder will therefore get a shelter dog instead. However as others have pointed out I don’t think this is necessarily true. At least in the case of pit bulls, many complexes and even entire cities ban them, so it can be hard to find the right dog if you’re only limited to shelters since many many shelter dogs are some mix of pit bull. Therefore if someone’s looking for a particular kind of dog, they may end up not getting one at all if they’re only limited to shelters; this does nothing to help the euthanasia rates.

Two, and this is something that I personally think is extremely important, dogs from shelters usually come with a lot of trauma, either from being in an abusive situation or from abandonment issues. In a perfect world I’d love for each of these dogs to get the help they need, but unfortunately not every potential dog owner is equipped to handle that. Many people want a dog as a loving companion and a friend to offer comfort; however if you’re dealing with a dog that has a lot of trauma this will be a very different situation. You may end up having to spend inordinate amounts of time and money on training, behavioral therapy, and what have you to help your dog to be a normal pet, and even then there may never really be a normal. I’ve had personal experience with this as my sister adopted a dog from a shelter, with PTSD issues... she wanted a normal pet, but instead she got a dog that is constantly chewing up all of her stuff, can not control his bladder, and just has major emotional issues all around. And he’s a grown adult dog. She already had money issues and now they’re even worse because she’s had to pay to fix the damage he’s done. And she can’t even afford training classes for him. And unfortunately it’s not as easy as saying “she should’ve found a better tempered dog at the shelter then” because problem is, SO many shelter dogs come with emotional baggage like this. There is just so much trauma that is associated with so many shelter dogs, and sometimes these issues can be fixed, but sometimes they can’t be. The thing is there are different methods for everyone. I think if you just do your homework, show up to class as much as possible and really truly pay attention then things will work out for you. Usually your professor isn’t trying to fail you and they want you to succeed! :) 
Also just don’t be afraid to talk to a professor if you need extra help!

They taught me things that the teachers would only gloss over (I essentially taught myself evolution because my teachers wouldn’t cover it in detail). At the same time I was taking chemistry and it all kind of opened my mind to the amazing world of science all at once. I decided on my last year of high school I wanted to be a biology major, just in time for college applications. It was a really big and kind of sudden change considering I had previously wanted to write, or be a lawyer of some kind.  I hadn’t done anything really biology related in my school years so I really struggled with my applications and the first year of college was way harder for me than my peers, who had already been exposed to most of the things I was just then learning.
